name: journey-tray
comment: Visibility Phase 2, Slice J1-Tray. Proves the app survives its real tray lifecycle and returns to the same user-visible page. Isolated tagged session, never the daily app. GROUND-TRUTH: production Colosseum ships no QSystemTrayIcon (grepped native/main.cpp -- no tray/SystemTrayIcon symbol exists), so there is no production minimize-to-tray affordance for the bridge to click; per J1-Tray-Bridge (window-set-state, landed 8a14059) this journey drives the window lifecycle directly via window-set-state, which calls the SAME real QWindow::showMinimized()/hide()/showNormal() API a titlebar minimize or a taskbar/tray restore would invoke in production -- never an OS-level tray-icon click (human-only, see human-tray-note.md). The named page is Biblio's Library tab (qml/BiblioWorld.qml's WorldTabBar, objectName 'biblioTabBar', tabPrefix 'biblioTab' -- distinct from Tankoban's 'worldTab' stem so the DFS name lookup can't collide, per WorldTabBar.qml's own header note). Page identity is biblioTabBar's own 'currentTab' property, bound directly to BiblioWorld's activeTab -- no test-only shadow state. GROUND-TRUTHED RACE (found live during this slice's own recon, 2026-08-14): biblioTabBar itself becomes visible before its tab-pill Repeater delegates finish building (the World Loader's asynchronous:true progressive build) -- an immediate ui-click/ui-query on a pill right after the tab bar's own visible flip can hit NO_SUCH_ITEM; every pill click below is preceded by a ui-wait-for on that pill's own visible property, exactly like the dock-settle pattern journey_open_manga.json already uses. GROUND-TRUTHED FACT (matches J1-Tray-Bridge's own header note on windowStateName()): after the FIRST minimize->restore, get-state reports windows.0.state as 'fullscreen', not 'normal' -- Colosseum's own WindowStatePolicy re-asserts its borderless-fullscreen chrome once the window is visible again. Every restore assertion below therefore checks visible==true AND state NOT IN {minimized,hidden}, never the literal string 'normal'. Two full cycles run in one session (regression: repeat minimize/restore twice) -- cycle 1 uses 'minimized' (the titlebar/taskbar-minimize analogue), cycle 2 uses 'hidden' (the tray-resident analogue, since a real tray icon would fully hide the window rather than leave a taskbar button) -- both are Drive-gated window-set-state calls, never an OS click. The scenario deliberately ENDS in a restored/visible state so the runner's own automatic session_stop (graceful WM_CLOSE via QProcess::terminate) exercises a clean stop from a visible window, not a minimized one.

one visible window, isolated data root, boot state recorded

sanity: Biblio opens on its default Discover tab
navigate to the deterministic named page for this journey: Biblio > Library
BASELINE: page identity established (biblioTabBar.currentTab == library)
BASELINE: window state before any lifecycle transition
CYCLE 1: minimize (titlebar/taskbar-minimize analogue)
CYCLE 1: the root window is genuinely minimized
CYCLE 1: restore
CYCLE 1: restored -- visible==true AND state is neither minimized nor hidden (NEVER asserted as the literal string 'normal' -- WindowStatePolicy re-asserts fullscreen chrome on restore)
CYCLE 1: same-page property UNCHANGED after restore
L2 layout verdict: the restored page is genuinely actionable, contained, and non-overlapping -- not merely present in state
CYCLE 2 (regression: repeat twice): hidden (tray-resident analogue -- a real tray icon fully hides the window rather than leaving a taskbar button)
CYCLE 2: the root window is genuinely hidden
CYCLE 2: restore
CYCLE 2: restored -- visible==true AND state is neither minimized nor hidden
CYCLE 2: same-page property STILL unchanged after a second lifecycle cycle
